text:
Alex: Heads-up — noticed p99 on the latency dashboard for /v1/generate spiked ~2x right after we enabled route fanout. Numbers look like they attributed to the 'client_tagged' rollup instead of the endpoint. Anyone seen this before?
Maria: hmm — did the rollout switch merge_mode to 'stitch_by_client'? We flipped routing yesterday.
Devon: Could be sampling origin getting reassigned. The console shows sample_source=route by default but fanout sets sample_source=client in fallback. Not sure how the percentile merge handles that.
Chris: here's the query I ran in the telemetry service:

``
SELECT percentiles(lat_ms, [50,95,99])
FROM requests
WHERE endpoint = '/v1/generate'
AND time > now() - 1h
GROUP BY rollup_tag(client_tag)
``

Results look like p99 for client_tag=mobile is huge but route-level p99 is smaller.
Pat: @Alex can you paste the dashboard config? if the dashboard is rollup_key=route, but the metric stream switched tags mid-rollout you can get double-counting.
Alex: config is default endpoint breakdown with rollup: ['route','client_tag'] — I didn't expect the p99 to flip attribution like that.
Jamie: Not double-counting, probably a merge-time attribution quirk. Our percentile merge assumes consistent origin; when origin flips we end up with smaller sample counts per bucket and t-digest merging yields higher p99. Essentially low-sample noisiness.
Maria: Got it. So we should either surface sample_count alongside percentiles or make the console warn when origin changes across the query window.
Devon: Agreed. Quick triage — add a badge showing sample_count and last_sample_origin for that timeseries, and a tooltip explaining t-digest low-count variance.
Chris: FYI I also pulled raw traces for the large p99s — they are 1–2 outliers from a single client. Sample_count for that client bucket was only 28.
Alex: ok sounds like UX + doc fix + alerting. Can we also add a backend check that if sample_origin is not stable for >10% of the window then mark percentiles 'unstable'?
Jamie: +1. We should also expose a 'composite' mode that stitches across origins by merging raw samples (expensive) and fall back to t-digest when cost cap reached. Backfill task created.
deploy-bot: deploy/rollout 2026-03-21T15:12:03Z — fanout-routing v2 rolled to 30% of traffic
Pat: action items: (1) Alex + Dev to add sample_count badge, (2) Maria to add console warning copy, (3) Jamie to prototype composite mode
Alex: I'll pick up (1) today. thanks all :thumbsup:
Maria: can we add a tiny 'why this moved' explainer in the widget? users keep opening tickets for p99 jumps.
Jamie: will draft short text. keep it <2 sentences. mention t-digest + sample origin.
Devon: logging note — when fanout flips origin we should emit telemetry.event:percentile_origin_change so dashboards can detect it.
Chris: good idea. I'll file a webhook + telemetry schema change.
Alex: thanks — ping me when PRs are ready, let's avoid another mid-rollout surprise.
